title: Async task pool
blurb: Run async work with a concurrency limit: ordered results, fail-fast or settle mode, and cancellation.
brief: Your team keeps hand-rolling the same loop: call an async function for every item in a list, but only a few at a time (uploads, API calls, file reads). Write it once, properly. Implement mapLimit in pool.js. The helpers in results.js are already done. Async code is where plausible-looking answers go wrong: timing, ordering and failure paths all matter, and the tests check each of them. There is no real clock here: tests settle each call by hand, so behavior must depend only on when your promises settle. Read your requirements closely and check what the assistant gives you.
requirements: mapLimit(items, limit, fn, { settle = false, signal } = {}). limit must be a positive integer (numbers only), otherwise throw RangeError. fn must be a function, otherwise throw TypeError. Both are thrown synchronously, not returned as a rejected promise.
items is any iterable; read it once, up front. Returns a promise for an array with one result per item, in input order, no matter which calls finish first. Empty input resolves to [].
fn(item, index) may return a plain value or a promise. At most limit calls are ever in flight, and the next item starts as soon as any call finishes (a sliding window, not fixed batches).
A synchronous throw from fn counts as a rejection of that call.
Fail-fast (settle false): on the first rejection, reject with that error and start no more calls. Calls already running are left alone; their later results or errors are ignored.
Settle mode (settle true): never rejects because of fn. Every item runs, and each result is fulfilled(value) or rejected(reason) from results.js, in input order.

signal is an AbortSignal-like object (aborted, reason, addEventListener, removeEventListener). If it is already aborted, reject with signal.reason without calling fn (even for empty input). If it aborts mid-run, start no more calls and reject with signal.reason (also in settle mode). Remove your abort listener once the promise settles, however it settles.
